skeleton:
Loubia b'Dersa — White Beans in the Garlic Emulsion

Tunisian · Easy · 6

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The loubia b'dersa is the #43 master's Tunisian-garlic dial — the same white bean pot, the same soak-and-slow-soften doctrine, but finished with the dersa: the raw garlic-and-cumin paste pounded to an emulsion and stirred into the beans' broth at the pot's end, its raw fire softened by the heat but never cooked away. This record carries the dersa's own law; the bean pot's architecture is the master's.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

- **The dersa's law: raw at the pound, tempered at the stir, never boiled.** The paste's garlic fires raw when pounded with the salt and the oil — that is its point — and the pot's own heat softens it to the rounded fire when stirred in off the flame. The dersa stirred in and boiled loses the whole register: the emulsion breaks, the garlic's edge deadens to the cooked-cloak's flatness. The off-heat stir is the record's single unbreakable law. - **The bridge:** the #43 master carries the bean doctrine (the soak's mercy, the bare simmer's hold, the broth's reduction); this seat carries the dersa — the same emulsion logic that finishes the Tunisian table's pasta and fish pots, the raw paste's tempering at the heat's edge.

Loubia b'Dersa — White Beans in the Garlic Emulsion

Prep: 15 min (plus 8 h soak) · Cook: 1 h 10 min · Total: 1 h 25 min · 6

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 300 g dried white beans (about 1½ cups), soaked 8 hours
  • 3 tbsp olive oil (about 40 g)
  • 1 onion (about 200 g), halved and sliced
  • 4 garlic cloves for the pot, plus 5 for the dersa
  • 2 tbsp tomato paste (about 30 g)
  • 1 tsp ground cumin, plus the dersa's own
  • ½ tsp harissa (#91), optional
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1.2 liters water
  • For the dersa: 5 garlic cloves (about 20 g), 1 tsp cumin seeds (about 3 g) toasted and ground, ½ tsp salt, 2 tbsp olive oil (about 25 g), and 2 tbsp of the beans' own broth
  • The finish: lemon juice and parsley

Instructions

  1. **The bean pot, per the #43 (about 1 hour).** The oil in the pot over medium; the onion softened 6 minutes, the 4 pot-garlic cloves for their minute, the tomato paste fried 30 seconds, the cumin and harissa bloomed in the paste's oil. The drained beans, water, and salt in; the barest simmer held, covered, until the beans run tender and the broth reduces to the loose sauce (the #43's own checkpoint: the bean's tooth-yield without the skin's burst). Checkpoint — the master's law: the surface never boils (the 90–95 °C hold) — the bean's skin's mercy and the broth's clarity both live at the shiver, and the rolling pot breaks both.
  2. **The dersa, while the beans finish (5 minutes).** The 5 dersa-garlic cloves pounded in the mortar with the ½ tsp salt to a paste; the toasted, ground cumin worked in; the oil added a thread at a time, the pestle's motion emulsifying to a thick, pungent cream — the beans' broth's 2 tablespoons stirred in at the end to loosen. Checkpoint — the dersa's proof: a smooth, holding emulsion — glossy and paste-creamy, not the mortar's scattered crush — and the smell: raw garlic's fire and the cumin's toast, forward and unapologetic. This paste is the pot's whole future; its rawness now is the finished flavor's own foundation.
  3. **The tempering stir — the record's hinge.** The pot off the flame entirely; the dersa stirred through the beans in the pot's own held warmth, the raw paste melting into the broth's body. Checkpoint — eating test: the bean's creamy-yield in the broth now run through with the garlic's rounded fire and the cumin's warm depth — the rawness tempered to the edge, still present, never cooked-flat — the lemon's squeeze and the parsley's green at the bowl's finish. It should taste like the #43's own bean pot with the Tunisian table's last-minute signature — the pot made an hour ago and finished thirty seconds ago, both truths in one bowl.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Dersa's fire absent, flatThe paste boiled inThe off-heat stir's law
Dersa's fire raw, aggressiveThe paste under-emulsifiedThe mortar's full pound; the broth's loosening
Beans' broth cloudy, skins burstThe pot boiled through the simmerThe #43's shiver law

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- Keeps 4 days refrigerated, the dersa's fire mellowing to the married depth by the second day — and the honest reheat's law: warmed to the steam's edge only, never the boil, or the dersa dies in the pot's second life. The variations: the fish's addition over the beans (the coastal Tunisian pot), the greens' winter fold, the fava's spring seat under the same dersa.
